[CANDIDATE] | web-review-001 | web-review | HIGH | security | src/api.js:16 | API base URL is hardcoded to a plaintext loopback address with no environment indirection | `baseURL: 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api'` literal at line 16; grep of src for `import.meta.env`/`VITE_` returned zero matches, so no build-time override exists | Every production bundle calls the developer machine; any HTTPS-hosted deployment is blocked as mixed content, and there is no HTTPS/TLS expectation anywhere | HIGH | high | security, config, deployment

[CANDIDATE] | web-review-003 | web-review | MEDIUM | security | src/App.jsx:30 | Route guard checks only token presence, never validity or expiry, so revoked/expired sessions still render protected UI | App.jsx:30 `const token = localStorage.getItem('token'); if (!token) return <Navigate .../>` — no expiry field, no `/api/user` probe, no storage event listener (grep found no addEventListener) | A stale token paints /tickets, /queue, /admin until the first 401; logout in one tab leaves other tabs showing an authenticated shell indefinitely | HIGH | medium | auth, correctness, stale-state
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-004 | web-review | MEDIUM | correctness | src/Login.jsx:72 | Login writes the token before validating the response shape, so a 200 without `token` stores the literal string "undefined" | Line 72 `localStorage.setItem('token', data.token)` has no guard; if `data.token` is undefined the stored value is the truthy string "undefined", which App.jsx:30 accepts and api.js:42 sends as `Bearer undefined` | Client guard is bypassed by a malformed/unexpected API response while every request 401s; user sees a logged-in shell that cannot load data and repeatedly hard-redirects via api.js:70 | HIGH | medium | correctness, auth, error-handling
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-005 | web-review | MEDIUM | reliability | src/api.js:13 | Axios instance defines no timeout, no cancel token, and no abort signal, so a hung backend leaves the UI permanently disabled | api.js:13-21 config has only baseURL/headers; grep for `timeout`, `signal`, `AbortController` in src returned no matches; Login.jsx:61 sets `loading=true` and :169 disables the submit button until `finally` at :93 | If the Laravel process hangs or the network stalls, the login button stays disabled forever with no retry and no message; Tickets/Admin have no loading state at all to distinguish empty from pending | HIGH | medium | reliability, ux, error-handling
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-006 | web-review | MEDIUM | correctness | src/Tickets.jsx:117 | Mutations derive new list state from the `tickets` closure captured at render instead of a functional updater, so concurrent responses clobber each other | Tickets.jsx:117 `setTickets([data, ...tickets])`, :142 and :159 `setTickets(tickets.map(...))`, :174 `setTickets(tickets.filter(...))`; same pattern at Admin.jsx:81, :98, :118 and :134 | Two in-flight actions (create + status change, or delete + assign) make the last writer win, resurrecting deleted rows or reverting just-saved edits until a manual refresh | HIGH | medium | correctness, stale-state, race-condition
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-007 | web-review | MEDIUM | correctness | src/Tickets.jsx:346 | `t.status.replace('_', ' ')` is called unguarded on server data, so a null/missing status throws during render with no error boundary | Tickets.jsx:346 dereferences `t.status` directly, while line 341 uses safe `t.category?.name`; main.jsx:6-10 mounts `<App />` inside StrictMode with no ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch (grep: no matches) | One malformed ticket record (FK/legacy row, partial payload, unexpected 200) throws in the list map and blanks the entire SPA with a white screen rather than degrading one row | HIGH | high | correctness, robustness, error-handling
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-008 | web-review | MEDIUM | correctness | src/Tickets.jsx:399 | Controlled status select is not reverted when the PATCH fails, so the DOM shows a status the server rejected | `<select value={t.status} onChange={handleStatusChange}>` at :399-407; handler :136-146 only calls setState on success, and on error just sets an alert string, so no re-render restores the old value; identical pattern for roles at Admin.jsx:275-286 | After a 403/422/network failure the dropdown displays the new status while data is unchanged; staff believe triage succeeded, and the mismatch persists until the page is reloaded | HIGH | medium | correctness, stale-state, error-handling
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-009 | web-review | LOW | error-handling | src/Tickets.jsx:86 | Loader uses Promise.all with a bare catch, discarding successful results and the real error message | :79-82 `Promise.all([api.get(url), api.get('/categories')])`; :86 `catch { }` binds nothing and replaces the server message with the fixed string "Could not load data. Is the API running?"; same shape at Admin.jsx:56-66 | A categories-only failure hides a successfully fetched ticket list, and the user/operator gets a misleading "API down" message that defeats diagnosis | HIGH | low | error-handling, ux
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-010 | web-review | LOW | race-condition | src/Admin.jsx:53 | Mount effect has no cancellation or ignore flag, so late responses can write state after unmount or after a second load starts | Admin.jsx:53-69 `load()` is called once with `[]` deps and no `let ignore=false`/AbortController guard; same in Tickets.jsx:69-93; StrictMode in main.jsx:7 double-invokes effects in dev, duplicating both GETs | Overlapping loads can interleave so an older snapshot wins the setState, and React logs state updates on unmounted components; on scope changes nothing prevents a stale response from overwriting fresh data | HIGH | low | race-condition, stale-state
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-011 | web-review | LOW | security | src/Tickets.jsx:226 | Unvalidated role string from localStorage is interpolated into a className, and Admin falls back to an "admin" label when the user object is missing | Tickets.jsx:226 `` className={`badge role-${me.role || 'user'}`} ``; Admin.jsx:171 uses `me.role || 'admin'`; same interpolation for server-supplied values at Tickets.jsx:345 `status-${t.status}` and :355 `priority-${t.priority}` | A crafted `role`/`status`/`priority` value injects arbitrary class tokens (style/DOM-attribute injection, no script execution) and Admin displays an admin badge to an anonymous-looking session, misreporting authorization state | MEDIUM | low | security, ui-injection, stale-state
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-012 | web-review | LOW | security | src/Admin.jsx:280 | Self-role-change protection relies on comparing server ids to the localStorage user object, so it is bypassable and type-fragile | `disabled={u.id === me.id}` at :280 with `me` parsed from localStorage at :42; a user editing `user` clears the guard, and a string/number id mismatch silently disables it for the real row | The only visible protection against self-demotion is cosmetic; it depends on client data the user controls, and a type mismatch produces an enabled control that always 403s | HIGH | low | security, auth, defensive-depth
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-013 | web-review | LOW | stale-state | src/Admin.jsx:131 | Role changes update only the in-memory users array, never the stored session user, so the acting admin and other users keep stale roles | :131-134 patches `/users/{id}/role` then `setUsers(...)`; localStorage `user` is untouched; Admin.jsx:294-298 and Tickets.jsx:45-48 document the lag; Tickets nav/controls read `me.role` at :58-59, :218-223 | A promoted agent sees no new controls and a demoted user keeps staff UI until re-login, so RBAC affordances drift from server truth and generate confusing 403s | HIGH | low | stale-state, auth, ux
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-014 | web-review | LOW | config | src/App.jsx:59 | Router has no basename while the 401 path hard-navigates to absolute "/", so subpath hosting breaks both routing and session-expiry redirects | `<BrowserRouter>` at App.jsx:59 with no basename; api.js:70 `window.location.assign('/')`; vite.config.js:5-7 sets no `base`; deep links require host-side SPA rewrite that is nowhere documented (README.md:1-16 is the stock Vite template) | Deploying at e.g. /helpdesk/ yields blank pages on refresh and a 401 redirect that leaves the app entirely, presenting as a total outage | HIGH | medium | config, deployment, routing
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-015 | web-review | LOW | security | index.html:3 | Document ships without a Content-Security-Policy or referrer policy, leaving no defense-in-depth for the localStorage token | index.html:3-8 contains only charset, icon, viewport, title; no CSP meta, no `referrer` meta, no SRI-bearing scripts, and index.css/main.jsx add no protections | With the token in localStorage (web-review-002), any injected script or compromised CDN asset runs unrestricted and can read and exfiltrate credentials; no compensating browser-level control exists | MEDIUM | medium | security, headers, defense-in-depth
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-016 | web-review | LOW | dependencies | package.json:13 | All runtime and build dependencies use caret ranges with no engines/packageManager pinning and no test tooling, so builds are non-reproducible and unverified | package.json:13-17 `^1.20.0`/`^19.2.8`/`^19.2.8`/`^7.18.4`, :18-28 devDeps `^8.3.0` vite etc.; installed tree already drifted to react 19.3.0 and vite 8.3.1; no `engines`, no `packageManager`, scripts :6-11 have no `test` | Fresh installs pull different majors of react-router (v7 breaking vs v6) and Vite 8 (needs Node >=20.19) on unstated Node versions; there is zero automated coverage of the auth guards and role gates | HIGH | medium | dependencies, reproducibility, supply-chain
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-017 | web-review | LOW | config | vite.config.js:5 | Dev/build config has no `/api` proxy and no env injection, which is why the client must hardcode the backend origin; no server hardening or build base is set | vite.config.js:5-7 contains only `plugins: [react()]`; no `server.proxy`, no `define`, no `base`, no `strictPort`, no `build` options | Local dev depends entirely on Laravel CORS being permissive, and there is no supported switch for staging/prod origins, directly enabling the hardcoded URL in web-review-001 | HIGH | low | config, dev-experience, deployment
[CANDIDATE] | web-review-018 | web-review | LOW | correctness | src/App.jsx:62 | Login route is unguarded for already-authenticated users, so a signed-in session can land on the credential form and overwrite its own token | `<Route path="/" element={<Login />} />` at App.jsx:62 has no inverse guard; Login.jsx:67-78 always posts and overwrites `token`/`user` on success; no `useEffect` redirect when a token exists | An authenticated user (or a link to "/") sees a login form, can accidentally replace a staff session with a customer token, and gets no logout affordance from that screen | HIGH | low | correctness, auth, ux
[CLEAN] | web-review | XSS sink obligation: dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, eval, new Function, document.write across src/*.jsx, index.html, src/index.css | Grep over src for those sink patterns returned only the api.js:16 baseURL and its comment; all user content renders as JSX text nodes (Tickets.jsx:336 title, :351 description, :362 requester name, Admin.jsx:272-273 name/email) which React escapes; index.css:247 uses only white-space: pre-wrap with no sanitizer bypass, so no DOM-XSS sink exists in this frontend
